title: Fluorescence Microscopy of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii - mCherry and Chlorophyll
author: João itor Molino
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kfrctm6

steps.title: Grow Chlamydomonas culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate Tris‑acetate‑phosphate (TAP) medium and grow cells to late‑log phase (~1 × 10⁷ cells/mL) at 25 °C with constant illumination of 50 μmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ while shaking at 150 rpm on a rotary shaker.

steps.title: Prepare agarose pad and mount cells
steps.instruction: Make a 1 % agarose TAP pad, add agarose to TAP medium, dissolve by microwaving, pour onto a slide that has a double‑adjacent‑slide barrier forming a wall, place a clean slide on top to flatten, then remove the top and barrier slides, spot 10 µL of the cultured cells onto the solidified pad, and cover with a coverslip.

steps.title: Image mCherry fluorescence
steps.instruction: Place the prepared slide on the fluorescence microscope, excite mCherry with an argon laser at 543 nm, set the spectral detector to collect emission between 610‑650 nm, and record the images.

steps.title: Image chlorophyll fluorescence
steps.instruction: Using the same slide, excite chlorophyll with a laser at 405 nm, set the spectral detector to 680 nm, and record the images.

steps.title: Acquire Z‑stack images
steps.instruction: For three‑dimensional imaging, acquire a Z‑stack using 0.4 µm step size between successive focal planes.
